searchText: So in case there is widespread outage on the AWS where many people are hosting ETH2, could that trigger a penalty on someone who is not using AWS also, right? Feels unfair. i don't think that's the case - in that i don't think there is an explicit penalty. it also depends on what % was using AWS if you remain online in such an outage, your balance will remain approximately neutral while those offline will begin to leak more and more (as long as not finalizing) So if less than 1/3 of the validators are offline, everyone gets penalized. If more than 1/3 are offline, then is the inactivity link case, right? Danny Ryan says this: *Inactivity penalty: if the chain isn’t finalising, penalize everyone, but particularly those who are not participating. Specifically, add a BASE_REWARD_PER_EPOCH * base_reward penalty to each active validator, and add an effective_balance * finality_delay // INACTIVITY_PENALTY_QUOTIENT penalty to each validator that did not vote on the correct target. Note that validators participating optimally during an inactivity leak will not incur any penalties [Potential bug discussed here].* https://notes.ethereum.org/@djrtwo/Bkn3zpwxB that might be worded imperfectly if you are doing your job perfectly during a leak, you should remain approximately neutral you can't gain here so that can be somewhat a "penalty". at least a call to action to do what is in your power to fix things OK that makes sense I mean in the extreme outage case, (correct me if I'm wrong) if that epoch happens to have a bunch of slots with empty(ish) beacon committees, the odds of you being selected as a beacon block proposer logically goes up. So you can* gain here technically no? Though I guess the down time would need to be significant (#validators*time) for proposer rewards to make any kind of real dent. AFAIK there's a special penalty for such cases, which is higher and will probably eat up all of your rewards however made you can gain from proposals during a leak so you can in some cases be profitable if you are relatively neutral for performing your attestation duties, then if you are selected for proposal, you can make a little bit of eth What if we just compensated the good validators after the crisis is over by just issuing eth to them? too crazy? if it was in fact a serious crisis and the leak happened for a long time, the total staking balance would be less and the rewards per staked eth will be higher if you reward success too much here, it would incentivize censoring/attacking some subset of validators to induce such a leak to begin with yes I can imagine when eth is very expensive, AWS employees with validators at home can pull a plug accidentally XD Or a few rug pulls from these centralized validator services issuing L1 [vapor]Beth between now and phase 1. On a different subject; do we have an estimate of how much a Slasher can potentially make? gotta be super subjective just curious Slasher counts as whistleblower, right? ^ got it. nothing for the slasher, for now. Not quite nothing, it’s about 0.0625 ETH per validator slashed for validators with effective balance 32. Assuming you run a slasher _and_ put the slashing in a block (which is what the Lighthouse slasher tries to do by default) If you broadcast and someone else includes it, then yeah it’s 0 <@!602753420033785856> lighthouse doesn't broadcast the slashing by default? No 😏 But I'm going to add an option to do that soon ah. well, you have to be pretty lucky then, since any broadcasting slasher that's running will... front-run you yeah, unless you see things on subnets that nobody else sees on Medalla I racked up 100s of slashings that nobody else got to but the incentives were very different and we hadn't released the LH slasher yet indeed, and I'm pretty sure not all clients were including slashings at all back then hopefully there won't be _any_ slashings on mainnet any time soon 🤞 haha true Or you could, you know, 😏 not make it the default option XD Perhaps the pyrmont launchpad should be fixed if it's going to continue running. Clients Discord's are being flooded with users confused by the meter not counting <@203220829473996800>'s 3M Goeth. <@602753420033785856> is the Lighthouse slasher using your hoarding technique? <@550420431744794624> may be able to update pyrmont launchpad **CarlBeek** I've been trying to avoid hacking in a solution to this, but I think it is time to give up hope on that cause. I'll see what I can do :) Currently, it is

excerpts.author: mohseng
excerpts.content: So if less than 1/3 of the validators are offline, everyone gets penalized.  If more than 1/3 are offline, then is the inactivity link case, right?  Danny Ryan says this:

excerpts.author: mohseng
excerpts.content: *Inactivity penalty: if the chain isn’t finalising, penalize everyone, but particularly those who are not participating. Specifically, add a BASE_REWARD_PER_EPOCH * base_reward penalty to each active validator, and add an effective_balance * finality_delay // INACTIVITY_PENALTY_QUOTIENT penalty to each validator that did not vote on the correct target. Note that validators participating optimally during an inactivity leak will not incur any penalties [Potential bug discussed here].*
